newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares decline, U.S. to determine way ahead.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares decline, U.S. to determine way ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Monday, reeling from Friday's Dow falls, with dealers seeing the next few days' trend being set by Wall Street.

"Friday's U.S. falls kept many players on the sidelines here today, waiting to see which way Wall Street is going. Tomorrow's market depends on events over there tonight and the upcoming Danish corporate first-half results," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index lost 1.13 point to close at 180.86 in overall bourse turnover of only 788 million crowns. The KFX September future fell 1.80 point to 180.00 with 878 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Danish cleaning group ISS and third biggest BG Bank, due to announce their first-half 1997 results on Tuesday, finished two and three crowns down respectively at 208 and 389.
Otherwise Sophus Berendsen ended the day eight crowns down at 942 ahead of its partly-owned British unit Rentokil's interim result on Tuesday.

On a more positive note biotechnological group Novo Nordisk recovered to close five crowns dearer at 697 after suffering falls on its first-half 1997 result last week. -Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969652
